MOD to meet the guest upon departure to check on them and reiterate the compensation. Guest had medicine delivered in the morning as they had a headache from the flickering lights and disrupted sleep. Guest had breakfast before they departed and relayed information to F&B team so they can show exceptional care of them. Greeted guest upon departure and extended sincere apologies for the inconvenience. Informed that I would be taking care of the room night and guest was appreciative and departed in much better spirits. (SK/FM/01MAR26)

rows.Incident Description: Housekeeping department reported to the Front Office Manager that a guest’s personal hair curling iron had been accidentally damaged by a room attendant during Make Up Room service earlier in the morning.
rows.Subject: 1000 | Ms. Hisako Tsujimoto | Hairdryer
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
At approximately 9:26 AM,  Housekeeping department reported to the Front Office Manager that a guest’s personal hair curling iron had been accidentally damaged by a room attendant during Make Up Room service earlier in the morning.

Actions Taken:
The Front Office Manager attempted to contact the guest immediately,  both via the guestroom phone and mobile phone. Attempts were unsuccessful.
An email was then sent to the guest to inform them of the incident and offer assistance.
The guest returned the call in the afternoon and spoke directly with the Front Office Manager.

Guest Communication & Resolution:
During the phone conversation,  the Front Office Manager apologized on behalf of the hotel and assured the guest that the hotel accepted full responsibility for the damage. The guest was offered the option of:

The hotel purchasing the exact brand/model of the curling iron they preferred,  or
The hotel providing a comparable model of equal quality.

The guest was invited to specify their preference at their convenience.
Later,  after further discussion,  the hotel proceeded to purchase a brand‑new hair curling iron along with a U.S.–Japan compatible adapter,  as agreed with the guest. The replacement items were delivered and placed in Room 1000.

Status:
✔ Issue fully resolved
✔ Replacement items delivered
✔ Guest has been informed and updated via email instead due to FOM could not reach out to guest both in room and mobile phone.

rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Upon departure,  the guest provided several pieces of feedback regarding service shortfalls experienced throughout her two-night stay. The concerns involved multiple departments including Housekeeping,  In‑Room Dining for Minibar,  and Ice Delivery. The guest expressed disappointment with slow service and compared her experience to a stay 25 years ago,  stating that service standards had been significantly better in the past.

Guest Concerns stated as below:

Slow Service Throughout the Stay
The guest reported consistent delays in various service requests across the two-night stay.

Housekeeping – Missing Replenishment

Lotion amenity was not replenished during the make‑up room service.

Ice Delivery Delay,  guest waited over 45 minutes for ice delivery. Due to the delay,  she cancelled the request and visited The Pen Top instead.

In-Room Dining Breakfast delivery was delayed (on the 1st night: 14 March)

Minibar – OJ Replenishment Not Completed when called to requested.
Guest requested orange juice to be replenished in the minibar the night before.
This request was not fulfilled.

Luggage Delivery Delay
Initial delay occurred because the guest provided the wrong room number.
After correcting the room number,  the guest expected a faster delivery and felt the service remained slow.

Expectation vs. Past Experience
Guest stated that service during her stay 25 years ago was “way better” than what she experienced this time.

Positive Guest Feedback:
The guest recognized and appreciated the following:
Laundry Department Service:
The dress pressing on the first day was “perfect.”
In-Room Dining Pre‑Order:
The pre‑ordered meal delivered on the morning of departure met expectations and was described as “great.”

Actions Taken

The Front Office Manager (FOM) personally apologized for all inconveniences experienced during the stay.
Explained to the guest that the issues raised are not reflective of The Peninsula’s service standards and assured that her concerns would be taken seriously.

As a gesture of goodwill,  the FOM offered:
A complimentary room upgrade for her next stay.
Direct point-of-contact details for future reservations to ensure a seamless experience.
The guest acknowledged the efforts,  accepted the gesture,  and departed the hotel in good spirits.

rows.Incident Description: On 31Mar26 at around 10:15 PM 1207 Mr. Mussafer approached the Front Desk requesting a cot to be placed in the room. FDA asked for the age of the additional guest, initially assuming a baby cot; the guest responded 30 indicating his adult daughter who was present with him. The FDA explained that the current room type would not accommodate an additional bed but advised that availability would be checked and the guest would be contacted if an alternative option could be arranged.
rows.Subject: 1207 | Mr. David Mark Mussafer | Room Assignment
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
⦁	At 10:20 PM,  the FDA called the guest and informed him that an extra bed could not be placed in the current room due to physical room limitations. A suite was offered as an alternative with a price difference. The guest declined the room move,  stated that he did not want to change rooms under any circumstances,  and became upset that a cot,  extra bed,  or additional bedding could not be provided. FDA explained that the intention was to offer the most comfortable solution and,  considering the one‑night stay and the guest’s repeat status,  extended a complimentary suite upgrade offer. The guest continued to refuse the move,  stated that this would be his last stay at The Peninsula,  and ended the call.
⦁	At 10:30 PM,  Mr. Mussafer called back and spoke with the FOM,  advising that his wife would be arriving at 12:30 AM and requesting that she be provided with a room key upon arrival. The guest was assured that this would be arranged. FOM apologized for the earlier inconvenience and again explained that the issue was related to the current room’s physical limitations and that additional bedding could not be placed. FOM also explained that alternative arrangements could have been explored earlier had the request been made prior to arrival,  Mr. Mussafer stated that his daughter was not initially planning to stay since she lives nearby but was later invited by him. He expressed that there was sufficient space in the room and stated that the situation was unacceptable,  noting that despite many previous enjoyable stays,  this would be their last stay at the hotel.
⦁	Given the guest’s heightened frustration,  no further calls were made; however,  Room 1512 was prepared with a sofa bed as a precaution should the guests decide to change rooms later.
⦁	Mrs. Mussafer arrived later and was welcomed by the FOM,  who apologized for the misunderstanding and informed her that a suite with an extra bed had been held should they feel uncomfortable in the current room. Mrs. Mussafer thanked for the arrangement but stated that they were likely already sleeping and expressed disappointment with the situation,  noting that they have been staying at the hotel for over 25 years.
⦁	Upon check out Mrs. Mussafer also stated that they ordered coffee in the morning but it was not delivered,  which later investigated with IRD that the order check was missed therefore it could not be delivered on time and guest declined to have it later. 
⦁	Guest has departed and apology email sent to the guest and FOM extended as Point of Contact 
⦁	Mr. Mussafer responded to the email stating that the incidents with the room and the coffee order unfortunate and he will not be coming back despite his loyalty for 20 years.
⦁ FOM responded to his email and stated that we will refund the charge for his accommodation as our apology and we hope to restore his trust in the future.
⦁ Total charge of $1.088, 17 is refunded to the guest

rows.Incident Description:
Summary of Events
Mr. and Mrs. Kim arrived for their scheduled 5:00 PM Suite 90-minute couple’s massage with Gene and William. Approximately 30 minutes into the service, Gene approached management to ask whether a female therapist was available to switch with her. I informed Gene that we were fully booked and no female therapist was available.
As an alternative, it was suggested that Gene and William switch clients to provide the guests with a different experience. This swap was completed approximately 30 minutes into the service.
Guest Concern
At approximately 6:00 PM, Gene requested that I speak directly with Mr. Kim due to his dissatisfaction. I met with Mr. Kim in the suite, where he expressed significant frustration with his massage experience with Gene. Mr. Kim stated that:
He has extensive experience receiving massages and felt Gene’s pressure was excessively firm.

Too much oil was used.

Adjustments were not made despite his requests.

The massage lacked flow and flexibility.

He felt Gene was not receptive to his preferences, which caused frustration and prevented him from relaxing.

Gene stated to Mr. Kim that he has 30 years of massage experience and that he did the best he could. This comment appeared to further aggravate Mr. Kim

Mr. Kim expressed that he was extremely satisfied with William’s service and enjoyed William’s technique. As a result, he asked that William work on his wife so that she could also experience William’s service. William and I coordinated so that Mr. Kim was later able to receive additional time with William as well.
Management Response
I sincerely apologized to Mr. Kim, listened attentively to his concerns, and offered accommodations to make him more comfortable, including food and additional hospitality. Mr. Kim declined further accommodations but thanked me for listening and addressing his concerns respectfully.
Upon completion of the service, William escorted Mr. and Mrs. Kim to the locker rooms to change.

Resolution
Before departure, I provided Mr. Kim with spa retail products for him to enjoy at his hotel, as he was visiting from Atlanta. I also gave him my business card and offered him a complimentary return visit to the spa, assuring him that we would provide an exceptional experience. I noted that William would be an ideal therapist for his future visit.
Staff Follow-Up
I spoke with Gene after the incident to discuss what could have been handled differently. Gene stated that he believed he adjusted pressure and responded to the guest’s concerns, but felt the guest was unable to relax regardless of changes made.
